what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to accept the April 2016 update of the comprehensive wastewater management plan, with the discussed additions, and take it to town meeting.
The commission voted to finalize and release the grease trap regulation change, after a hearing that also drew public questions on fees and timing.
The commission voted to use the invitation-for-bid process for the next operations and maintenance contract, then approved the bid with transitional support at the contract rate table.
The commission voted to reassess a Twin City betterment from one parcel to the correct parcel.
The Twin City waiver request was referred: staff are to ask for the plumbing inspector's sign-off before any waiver is granted.

why_it_matters: The grease trap rules move permit fees to a two-tier structure for internal and external traps, which can change what food businesses pay and is meant to keep grease costs off homeowners' sewer bills.
The wastewater plan going to town meeting carries betterment estimates by service area, so residents may be asked to vote on a plan that leads to betterment charges on property tax bills.
Bidding the operations contract sets who runs the sewer system and at what rate, which feeds into future sewer rates.
watch_next: The wastewater management plan update at town meeting.
Staff follow-up on the Twin City plumbing inspector sign-off before the waiver is granted.
